To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the voltage-dependent conformation change in the channel pore is the trigger for the depolarization-induced nuclear signaling via the ERK-CreB pathway.
the voltage-gated Ca2+ channel Cav1.3 mediates depolarization-induced nuclear activation in a Ca2+ influx independent manner, by a mechanism that involves the channel pore occupancy.
ET coupling in Cav1.3 transfected HEK-293 cells is triggered by membrane depolariation via a Ca2+ influx independent pathway.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of ET coupling, and the molecular mechanism of how the L-type Ca2+ channel can drive nuclear activity.
the molecular mechanisms of the depolarization-triggering signaling pathway from the voltage-gated Ca2+ channel to gene expression.
the molecular mechanisms that underlie the coupling between electrical activity and gene expression in the central nervous system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the voltage-gated Ca2+ channel Cav1.1 is a Ca2+-influx independent channel.
Ca2+ influx is not required for triggering ET coupling.
ET coupling in the absence of extracelluar Ca2+ is triggered by the voltage-gated Ca2+ channel pore occupancy and that the ERK-CreB pathway is the main signaling cascade for ET coupling.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Ca2+-influx-independent ET coupling is mediated by the voltage-gated Cav1.2 calcium channel.
the voltage-gated Ca2+ channel is a metabotropic receptor for depolarizing stimuli, and that ET coupling is driven by the CaMKII and ERK-CRE pathways.
the Ca2+/CaM-dependent pathway and the Ca2+/ CaM-independent pathway are both involved in the ET coupling.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ion-influx-independent function of Cav1.3 is a general mechanism for the conversion of synaptic signals to nuclear activity in excitable cells.
the ion-influx-independent function of Cav1. 2 in triggering ET coupling is mediated by a voltage-sensitive conformational change of the Cav1.2 channel pore.
ET coupling is not mediated by Ca2+/calmidulin-dependent pathways.
